summary.headline: Two clear favorites, one safety, one to watch
body: Juniper Lane and the Clay & Paint Studio School both teach the way you described: teachers build on what children are already doing, and art is the main way children explore ideas. Juniper Lane is the safer institution. The Studio School is the closer match in the classroom but runs thin on cash.

Dolores Park Cooperative is the most affordable and has the best ratios, but the co-op shifts do not fit two in-office parents. Treehouse Montessori is strong on paper and on kindergarten placement; tour it to see whether the Montessori work cycle feels right for Nia.

Two free options are on the list too. Marigold Elementary's TK is free and walkable for 2028-29, when Nia turns four, so it could replace a second paid preschool year. Sunrise Head Start is free for families who qualify; it is worth a call to check.

recommendation.why: Best overall: the teaching style you want, a ten-year average teacher tenure, and a year of cash in reserve.
The closest classroom match, a four-minute walk. Apply early: admission is rolling, so timing counts.
Strongest kindergarten placement record. Tour before deciding whether the approach fits.
Keep only if one parent can take a weekly classroom shift.

essays.draft:
Nia is a talker. She narrates whatever she is building, and when something falls over she tells us exactly what went wrong and what she will try next. She is cautious with new people for the first few minutes, then she is the one handing out jobs.

We were drawn to Juniper Lane because of how the teachers play alongside the children and then step back. [A MOMENT FROM THE TOUR]. That is how Nia learns best at home: when someone shows her one step and lets her take the next.

At home we speak English and Yoruba, and she switches between them depending on who she is talking to. [SOMETHING SHE LOVES TO MAKE].

Nia thinks with her hands. Give her clay or a box of buttons and she will tell you a story about it. [HER FAVORITE MATERIAL].
